experiments.title: Every article has a date it can defend — page-date probe + stale gate on the established shows

experiments.title: Item coverage floor reads each item's own Source and runs on flagged gates
experiments.baseline: Item coverage on the last 4 episodes of each established news show: Tesla 25-67%, SpaceX 0-43%, FF 7-33%, M&A 0-46%, Omni View 0%, MIT 0-20%, MAB 0-100%; the floor added 1 verified claim in 24 episodes. The repair call answered [] on Tesla Ep624 and SpaceX Ep120 (2026-10-04 logs): it asked for a page from memory. 4 of those 24 (and 3 of Planetterrian's last 4) were still failing after the first repair and got no floor at all.
experiments.target: source_integrity_item_coverage_pct median >= 50 on Tesla, SpaceX, M&A, Omni View and MIT over 14 days; coverage_repair_added > 0 on >= 60% of the episodes where the floor ran; the network claims page's verified share does not fall.
experiments.criteria: Hit = all three. coverage_repair_grounded high but _added near 0 = the model will not quote (read the "item coverage floor" log line's offered / rejected counts before touching the prompt); grounded low = the run's fetched copy is thin on those shows (fetch_full_text), not the floor. A verified-share drop means added entries are failing on re-verification and the floor is not only adding.
experiments.notes: Replay without the model on six Oct 3-4 flagship digests: 29 of 43 uncovered sourced items got a passage from their own Source URL by HTTP alone (the runner also holds the fetched copy). The mechanical check is unchanged; entries are added only when each verifies, and the result is kept only when the gate verifies more and gets no worse. experiments.title: Publish and mark: on_failure flag on every show, nightly re-verification, public claims ledger

experiments.criteria: Hit = all four. A verified_later rate under 20% = the unreachable class is mostly runner-blocked publishers, so the nightly needs a second egress or the fetch-cache corpus; a verified share under 75% = the ledger is thin (the empty-ledger class), not the policy. Any flagged claim later shown FALSE by a reader report = file the correction (the mechanism exists) and read the reason mix before changing the policy; one false flagged claim is not a reason to return to stripping true ones.

experiments.title: Story-driven scene briefs — the pictures follow the narration
experiments.target: Viewer complaints about imagery not matching the subject stop; long-form hold at 5% and Shorts AVP up. Mechanism: one Grok text call per episode writes a concrete, photographable scene per STORY (engine/scene_briefs.py); those briefs LEAD every Grok Imagine prompt (the static image_queries — 'cybertruck', 'supercharger' — used to lead, so every Tesla episode shipped the same four pictures); one fresh 16:9 scene per story (cap 8, was a fixed 4) keyed to its chapter for the scheduler; the library blend is back to 8 and ON-TOPIC ONLY (>=1 shared token with hook + chapter titles) instead of padding with random older images.
experiments.notes: Cost: +~4 images/episode at $0.02 (+$0.08/ep, ~+$30/mo network) + one ~$0.005 text call. Per-show opt-out scene_briefs_enabled; counts via scenes_per_episode / short_scenes_per_episode. Render/metadata only (outside landmine #17). First A/B-eyeball: compare a tesla + spacex + FF episode's scenes_ep*/ against the digest headlines. 2026-09-09 EARLY READ (lag-aware, 09-03..06 vs 08-27..31; several changes landed together, so this is a joint read with hook-first titles and the 2K sources): EN views/day roughly doubled (WoW +55.7%, 15,680 vs 10,070), RU +17.1%, Shorts AVP EN 43 -> 50% (median), FR 44 -> 52%; per-video EN long 30 -> 78 views, EN Short 12 -> 25. Biggest movers: MAB Shorts 10 -> 227 views/video, Planetterrian Shorts 9 -> 287, FF long 28 -> 116, SpaceX long 80 -> 277. Long-form AVP did NOT move (EN 14 -> 10-14%) and the open cliff sits at 0.48-0.49 hold at 5% — the retention metric this entry is scored on is still the open question for 09-23.

experiments.title: 2K source images + Shorts open on the scene about THEIR story
experiments.target: Sharper stills (the 16:9 render prescales to 3840 wide for Ken Burns; a 1792-wide source was a 2.1x upsample before any zoom — the softness viewers describe); every Short now leads with the fresh scene whose brief best matches its own window text instead of whichever scene was generated first. Reads jointly with scene-briefs-narrative-imagery on Shorts AVP + long-form hold.
experiments.notes: Request size ladder 2K -> legacy -> none, so a revision rejecting 2K can never cost an image (guarded). Zero extra cost at the standard model. DECISION for the operator (separate, cost-bearing): grok_image_model: grok-imagine-image-quality ($0.05 vs $0.02) on the three engine shows (FF, spacex, tesla) ≈ +$35/mo — the honest next step if 2K + story briefs don't end the complaints. 2026-09-03 CORRECTION: the 2K `size` request was a NO-OP — the endpoint ignores `size`; every one of the 7,500+ committed gallery sidecars (dimensions probed from the real bytes) is 1280x720 / 720x1280 on grok-imagine-image whatever was requested. Replaced by the documented `aspect_ratio` + `resolution: "2k"` fields (video-quality-round-3). The delivered width is now recorded per episode as grok_image_px_max; the first honest 2K episodes are 2026-09-03's — 1280 there means the endpoint ignored the documented field too and the quality-tier decision moves up. 2026-09-09 READ: the documented fields WORK — every image since the 09-03 slate is 2816x1584 / 1584x2816 (gallery sidecars, probed from the bytes; was 1280x720 for three months). The 16:9 render's 3840-wide prescale is now a 1.36x upsample instead of 3x.

experiments.title: Grok 4.6 -> 4.7, staged (operator-directed)
experiments.baseline: Eleven production sites run grok-4.6: the episode reviewer and the weekly synthesizer (network defaults), three shows' SCRIPT stage (omni_view, models_agents_beginners, dp_pod), the spacex deep-dive model, the YouTube title bundle (3 call sites), and the translation pin. A twelfth — the topic-queue restock — was pinned AWAY from 4.6 to grok-4.3 on 2026-09-17 after 4.6 timed out at 300s on both shows in one dispatch. Digest and fetch stages network-wide stay on grok-4.3 and are NOT in scope.
experiments.target: Day one moves exactly two sites, per docs/model_upgrade_playbook.md rule 1: the episode reviewer (outside run_show's timeout envelope, daily on every show, nothing a listener hears) and omni_view's script stage (one show, script-only — the shape the playbook calls correct). Three scheduled days, then `python scripts/model_trial_report.py --since 2026-09-22` must return GATE: PASS before anything widens.
experiments.criteria: REVERT TRIGGERS ARE OPERATIONAL FIRST, which is the whole lesson of the 2026-08-18 outage — its registered triggers watched hallucination rate and reviewer flags, and nobody watched latency, so the failure that actually fired was unmonitored. Revert if ANY of: an LLM stage's p95 exceeds 50% of the request timeout; an LLM stage p95 regresses more than 50% against its trailing-14-day baseline; any `Slow LLM completion` warning appears in the staged show's logs; any run fails or is skipped for a timeout. Only then quality: a listener-value regression on omni_view, or a reviewer that stops finding what the 4.6 reviewer found. Widening order once the gate passes: models_agents_beginners + dp_pod script stages, then synth_model, then the YouTube title bundle and the translation pin, then the spacex deep-dive; the restock is the natural place to test whether 4.7 fixed the latency that disqualified 4.6.
experiments.notes: Same list price as 4.6 (operator), so a widening is a quality and latency decision and never a cost one — priced in engine/tracking.py before any stage used it (playbook rule 4). The reviewer carries a trap this migration nearly walked into: review_episodes.py forced reasoning_effort "low" on a `grok-4.6` prefix match, because at default effort 4.6 blew the 300s timeout on ~1/3 of episodes and killed the audit job. Pinned to one id, the 4.7 pin would have matched nothing and silently restored default effort. That branch is now a prefix tuple. omni_view's script change is AUDIO — A/B-listen the first episode (landmine #17). Rollback is one line per site.

experiments.title: Content-density pass — scripts written from the digest, not copied; one owner per fact
experiments.baseline: flagship scripts 44-66% median digest-verbatim 8-grams (SpaceX 66, Tesla 49, M&A 44); 33 cross-section duplicate digest items in 160 digests; filler 6-10% of sentences on SpaceX; deep dive re-told a covered story in 5/6 M&A episodes
experiments.target: script_digest_overlap_pct <= 25% on every flagship episode; digest_cross_section_dupes_removed trending to 0; script_filler_pct <= 5%; one closing text per flagship on 10/10. Read from the review_snapshot "Script density audit" table and metrics_ep*.json.
experiments.criteria: Hit = all four numbers move as targeted on the three flagships by the readout. Partial (verbatim share does not move but duplicates and filler do) = ship the data-side paraphrase gate (reject + one script rerun above threshold). Miss on any A/B-listened prompt = git revert of that prompt only; the engine modules stay (removal-only, read-only).
experiments.notes: Operator brief 2026-09-05 ("narrative driven with redundant repetition"). Every prompt change is landmine-#17 A/B; the engine changes (engine/digest_overlap, engine/script_audit, show_memory instruction, pronunciation, duplicate tail-line guard) are not. Review doc: docs/reviews/network_delivery_review_2026_09_05.md. Same-day readout (Tesla Ep595 vs Ep596): filler 3 -> 0, verbatim only 63% -> 51%, so the script rewrite gate shipped the same evening (llm.script_rewrite_gate_overlap_pct = 40 on the nine English news shows). Score the verbatim target against script_rewrite_gate_after_pct where the gate fired. Sep 12: the rewrite gate was REMOVED (Sep 9-12: 30/35 fired, 11 accepted, 17 rejected as facts_lost / names_lost / copies_more - a script could be written OR complete, never both, because the script stage re-told a finished document). Superseded by combined-generation-2026-09-12; score this entry's targets on script_digest_overlap_pct + script_digest_coverage_pct from the combined episodes instead.

experiments.title: One generation — digest and script written in the same model call
experiments.baseline: two-pass: first drafts 55-77% digest-verbatim with 85-97% coverage; rewrites 1-4% verbatim with 40-60% coverage (Sep 9-12, nine gated shows); one extra script call per gated episode

Partial = combined ships but coverage stays under 70% -> tighten the PART-2 bridge wording (A/B), never re-add a retry. Miss = fallback rate > 50% or a lost episode -> llm.combined_generation: false in _defaults.yaml (one line).
experiments.notes: docs/reviews/simplification_plan_2026_09_12.md Phase B. The script stage used to re-tell a finished document; the Sep 5-9 rewrite gate (removed in the same pass) proved no retry could make it both written and complete. Narrative, dialogue, prompt-chained, script-model-override and episode-1 runs stay two-pass by code; the Russian shows pin the flag off. First live combined slate is the A/B-listen set (landmine #17): the podcast prompt is rendered with PART-1 placeholders for the digest and hook. Chain no longer excludes (09-17); M&A combined 38-59% overlap / 72-84% coverage, so the bridge now asks for spoken register + section names (A/B). Re-score 09-24.

experiments.title: Source-integrity enforcement on every show — strip the sentence, keep the day
experiments.baseline: shadow mode would have blocked SpaceX 2/7, Tesla 2/7, FF 4/7, PT 4/7, MIT 1/7 of the last seven episodes (malformed ledger entries, one uncovered shape on empty-ledger episodes, 403s) - none a proven fabrication; UC blocked 5x/14d
experiments.target: source_integrity_passed_after_strip = true on >= 95% of news-show episodes; 0 news-show skips with reason source_integrity_failed; source_integrity_stripped_sentences median <= 2 per stripped episode; source_integrity_script_stripped_sentences tracks the digest number (the script no longer carries a sentence the digest lost).
experiments.criteria: Hit = no lost news day and every published digest passed the mechanical gate. Partial = strips are frequent (> 3 sentences on > 20% of episodes) -> the prompt's claims appendix is the fix (A/B), not a looser gate. Miss = an unverified citation ships or a whole story is routinely stripped -> on_failure: block per show.
experiments.notes: Phase C of the simplification plan. source_integrity.on_failure (block | strip) - the narrative shows keep block. An uncovered citation shape whose item carries a resolving Source URL counts as sourced by the item (source_integrity_covered_by_item_source). Reviewer-note parentheticals are removed, their sentence kept. HOOK / header lines are never edited: a failure there still blocks. Sep 17 readout: 0 news-show blocks, 20/20 stripped episodes passed, median strip 1 sentence - every removal an UNREACHABLE source (x.com, 403 journals) whose text the fetch stage already held. Claims now verify against the fetched copy first (verified_from_fetched); sidecars record stripped_sentences. PT stripped 5/5 days is the baseline to beat.

Revert = restore the previous COLD text and drop the budget block; the voided-pick drought fix stays either way.
